domain.purpose: EPTTS Mobile is the mobile application (Android & iOS, package com.daf.eda.eptts) for the Egyptian Pharmaceutical Track & Trace System, operated by the Egyptian Drug Authority (EDA). It enables the serialized-pharmaceutical supply chain — Manufacturer to Distributor to Branch to Pharmacy to Patient — to receive, sell/dispense, return, and trace GS1-serialized product packs (SGTIN) and containers/cases (SSCC), and submits every action as an EPCIS event to the national EPTTS registry (backend referred to as 'Masar'). The app opens to an EDA-branded landing screen with two entry points: 'Sign In' (Keycloak-based role login for staff — Pharmacy, Branch, Distributor, Inspector) and 'Patient' (public, unauthenticated access for consumers to verify a dispensed pack). Each staff role gets a different tile-based home screen and feature set, determined server-side by the login credentials, not chosen client-side.

roles.name: Pharmacy
roles.permissions: Last point in the supply chain before the patient. Logs in with a pharmacy account (e.g. sydybishresaaf@eptts.com); the pharmacy's registered GLN entity name is shown in the home header (e.g. 'PH Sydy Bishr esaaf 24'). Home screen has 6 tiles: Receive Invoice (accept incoming shipments from a distributor/branch by scanning packs against the invoice manifest), Dispense (scan a pack to record dispensing to a patient — terminal EPCIS event, removes pack from inventory), Return Pack (pharmacy-to-upstream return: scan pack/SSCC + optional note + Initiate Return, goes to distributor/manufacturer), Branch Return (accept an incoming return sent from a branch back into pharmacy inventory), My Returns (history of returns the pharmacy initiated; statuses PENDING/CONFIRMED/CANCELLED), and EPCIS History (event log: SHIPPING/RECEIVING/UNPACKING/DISPENSING, Completed/Failed status, tap a Failed card to view an error bottom sheet with error code e.g. INTEGRITY_ERROR).

roles.name: Branch
roles.permissions: Warehouse/storage facility intermediary between distributor and pharmacies. Logs in with a branch account (e.g. testbranch@eptts.com); header shows 'Hello / <Branch name>' e.g. 'Main warehouse'. Home screen has 7 tiles: Create Shipment (Destination GLN autocomplete + ERP Invoice Number -> Create Draft -> scan packs -> dispatch), My Shipments (list + Shipment Details with Cancel Shipment for Dispatched status), Receive Shipment (Incoming Invoices list -> scan screen with progress bar, receives from manufacturers and distributors), Returns (sub-menu: Manufacturer Return / My Returns / Incoming Returns — incoming returns come from pharmacies and require Confirm Return or Cancel Return while PENDING), EPCIS History, Delete Account (destructive, requires confirmation), and Logout (requires confirmation dialog). Shipment statuses: Draft, Dispatched, Delivered, Partially Delivered.

roles.name: Distributor
roles.permissions: Mid-chain supply entity: bulk receipt from manufacturers, onward distribution to branches/pharmacies. Logs in with a distributor account (e.g. testdistributor2@eptts.com). Home screen has 5 tiles (no Delete Account/Logout tiles surfaced on home grid in captured build): Create Shipment (same Destination GLN + ERP Invoice Number flow as Branch), My Shipments (statuses Draft/Dispatched/Delivered/Partially Delivered, Cancel Shipment on Dispatched), Receive Shipment (list titled 'Incoming Invoices'; opening an item shows page titled 'Receive Shipment' with scan progress, Scanned/Remaining tabs), Returns (sub-menu: Manufacturer Return [blue, scan + optional note], My Returns [green, CONFIRMED/CANCELLED], Incoming Returns [yellow/tan, PENDING/CANCELLED, from pharmacies/branches — Confirm Return/Cancel Return actions while PENDING]), and EPCIS History (SHIPPING/RECEIVING/UNPACKING events; Failed events open an error bottom sheet, not a new page). Access token expires every 15 minutes and the app does not auto-refresh (shows 'Unauthorized' + a non-functional Retry button) — user must logout/login again.

roles.name: Inspector
roles.permissions: Read-only regulatory/government auditor role on behalf of the EDA, with visibility across ALL supply-chain parties (manufacturer, distributor, branch, pharmacy). Logs in with an inspector account (e.g. testinspector@eptts.com); header shows the Keycloak account/entity name (e.g. 'System Admin Entity'). Home screen has 4 tiles in a 2x2 grid: View Shipments (browse all shipments across all parties, read-only; list shows invoice #, sender, pack count, date, status — Dispatched/Partially Delivered/Delivered/Draft; detail view has From/To/Items/Packs/Dispatched/Created and a View Invoice action, no drill-down on line items), Trace (two tabs — Pack [SGTIN, hint 'Enter SGTIN (GTIN + Serial)'] and Container [SSCC, hint 'Enter SSCC'] — with an optional entity filter, camera scan or manual entry, and a Trace button returning the full custody-transfer event history for that pack/container), Delete Account (destructive, confirmation required), and Logout (confirmation dialog: 'Are you sure you want to logout?' with Cancel/Confirm). Inspector cannot create, modify, accept, reject, or delete shipments, packs, or returns — strictly read-only/investigative.

roles.name: Patient
roles.permissions: Public, unauthenticated role — no login/Keycloak SSO required. Accessed via the 'Patient' button on the landing screen. Single-tile home screen: Validate Pack, which opens a camera-based GS1/SGTIN barcode scanner; scanning a pack shows inline validation results (authenticity + supply-chain status). Cannot view shipments, returns, or EPCIS history — verification only. Back navigation returns to the landing screen.

entities.name: Pack (SGTIN)
entities.description: A single serialized pharmaceutical unit identified by a GS1 SGTIN (GTIN + Serial Number) barcode/DataMatrix code. Tracked through receive, dispense, return, and trace flows; carries an inventory/custody state (e.g. in a pharmacy's stock, dispensed, returned).

entities.name: Container/Case (SSCC)
entities.description: A logistics unit (case/pallet) identified by an SSCC code, grouping multiple packs together for shipment or return purposes; traceable separately from individual packs via the Inspector Trace 'Container' tab.

entities.name: Shipment/Invoice
entities.description: An outbound or inbound consignment of serialized packs between two GLN entities (e.g. Distributor to Pharmacy). Created as a Draft (Destination GLN + ERP Invoice Number), then packs are scanned in, then it is dispatched. Statuses: Draft, Dispatched, Delivered, Partially Delivered. Received via 'Incoming Invoices' list -> scan-to-confirm flow with a live progress bar (X/Y packs, Scanned/Remaining tabs).

entities.name: Return
entities.description: A request to move one or more packs backward in the supply chain (e.g. Pharmacy to Distributor, Branch to Manufacturer, Pharmacy to Branch). Created by scanning a pack/SSCC plus an optional free-text note and tapping Initiate Return. Numbered RET-YYYY-NNNNNN (sequential) or AGENT-RTB-<UUID> (agent-generated). Statuses: PENDING, CONFIRMED, CANCELLED. PENDING incoming returns must be Confirmed or Cancelled by the receiving party before they expire; CANCELLED returns cannot be reactivated.

entities.name: EPCIS Event
entities.description: An Electronic Product Code Information Services record submitted to the national EPTTS registry for every supply-chain action. Types observed: SHIPPING, RECEIVING, UNPACKING, DISPENSING. Each event has a UUID/hash identifier, sender, receiver, item count, event time, and a status of Completed or Failed. Failed events show a 'View event errors' affordance that opens a bottom sheet with per-sequence error code (e.g. INTEGRITY_ERROR) and error message (e.g. 'SSCCs not found in system: <SSCC>').

entities.name: GLN Entity
entities.description: Global Location Number — uniquely identifies a supply-chain party (pharmacy, branch, distributor, manufacturer) used as the searchable Destination field when creating shipments and as From/To fields on shipments and returns. Example GLNs observed: 6224010009998, 5413868000009, 6224010004313.

entities.name: User Account / Role
entities.description: A Keycloak-authenticated account whose role (Pharmacy, Branch, Distributor, Inspector) is determined server-side; the account's entity/GLN name is displayed in the home-screen header. Access tokens expire after 15 minutes with no auto-refresh (app shows 'Unauthorized' with a non-functional Retry button until the user logs out and back in).

domain.workflows:
1) Launch & Landing: App opens to an EDA-branded landing screen with 'Sign In' (primary) and 'Patient' (secondary) buttons.
2) Sign In (all staff roles): Landing -> Sign In -> enter username/password (Keycloak WebView) -> Login. The app routes to a role-specific home screen based on server-side role resolution; UI/tiles differ per role. Session tokens expire after 15 minutes with no silent refresh — an 'Unauthorized' state with a broken Retry button appears, requiring logout and re-login.
3) Pharmacy flow: Login -> Pharmacy Home (6 tiles) -> Receive Invoice (pick an Incoming Invoice -> scan each pack -> progress bar fills -> confirm) OR Dispense (scan one pack -> validate in-stock -> confirm -> pack marked dispensed, EPCIS DISPENSING event) OR Return Pack (scan pack/SSCC -> optional note -> Initiate Return -> appears in My Returns) OR Branch Return (accept an incoming return from a branch -> scan packs -> confirm receipt into inventory) OR My Returns (view own return history/status) OR EPCIS History (view/filter event log, inspect Failed event errors in a bottom sheet).
4) Distributor/Branch flow (near-identical): Login -> Home (5 tiles for Distributor, 7 for Branch incl. Delete Account + Logout) -> Create Shipment (search/select Destination GLN -> enter ERP Invoice Number -> Create Draft -> scan packs into the draft -> dispatch) OR My Shipments (list with statuses; Cancel Shipment available while Dispatched) OR Receive Shipment (Incoming Invoices list -> open -> scan all packs against manifest -> confirm, may result in Partially Delivered) OR Returns sub-menu: Manufacturer Return (scan + optional note + Initiate Return), My Returns (own outgoing return history), Incoming Returns (returns received from downstream parties; PENDING items require Confirm Return or Cancel Return) OR EPCIS History (SHIPPING/RECEIVING/UNPACKING events, Failed-event bottom sheet detail).
5) Inspector flow (read-only): Login -> Inspector Home (2x2 grid: View Shipments, Trace, Delete Account, Logout) -> View Shipments (browse all parties' shipments -> tap a card -> Shipment Details with View Invoice action, no line-item drill-down) OR Trace (choose Pack [SGTIN] or Container [SSCC] tab -> optional entity filter -> scan or type the code -> tap Trace -> full custody-transfer event history returned) OR Logout (tile -> 'Are you sure you want to logout?' dialog -> Confirm/Cancel).
6) Patient flow (no auth): Landing -> Patient -> Patient Home (single 'Validate Pack' tile) -> tap Validate Pack -> camera scanner opens -> scan a GS1/SGTIN barcode -> inline validation result (authenticity + supply-chain status) shown -> Back returns to Patient Home, Back again returns to Landing.
7) Shared/cross-cutting: Logout (tile -> confirmation dialog -> Confirm logs out to Landing, Cancel dismisses) is present for Branch/Distributor/Inspector; Delete Account is a destructive action gated by a confirmation dialog, present for Branch/Inspector home screens. All scan-driven flows (receive, dispense, return, trace, validate) use a shared scanner component (camera-based, GS1/SGTIN or SSCC) with real-time progress (X/Y, Scanned/Remaining tabs) where multiple packs are involved.

glossary.meaning: Egyptian Pharmaceutical Track & Trace System — the national serialization/track-and-trace program run by the EDA that this app supports.
Egyptian Drug Authority (هيئة الدواء المصرية) — the regulatory authority operating EPTTS.
Name used in the FRs for the backend system that transactions are synchronized/submitted to.
Global standards body defining the barcode/identifier formats (GTIN, SGTIN, SSCC, GLN) used throughout the app.
Global Trade Item Number — identifies a product/pack type (not a unique serial instance).
Serialized GTIN — GTIN + a unique serial number, identifying one specific physical pack; used for Dispense, Return, and Trace-Pack flows.
Serial Shipping Container Code — identifies a logistics container/case grouping multiple packs; used in Trace-Container and return flows.
Global Location Number — uniquely identifies a supply-chain party/location (pharmacy, branch, distributor, manufacturer); used as Destination/From/To fields on shipments and returns.

Electronic Product Code Information Services — the event standard/log (SHIPPING, RECEIVING, UNPACKING, DISPENSING) submitted to the national registry for every supply-chain action; viewable per role in 'EPCIS History'.
The SSO/identity provider used for staff Sign In (WebView-based login); the Patient flow bypasses it entirely.
The Android/iOS application package identifier for EPTTS Mobile.
The 2D barcode format printed on pharmaceutical packs encoding GTIN + serial (+ batch/expiry per GS1 AI standard), read via camera scan or physical scanner.
A return flow (Distributor/Branch) sending packs back up the chain to the manufacturer.
Pharmacy-side flow accepting a return sent down from a Branch back into pharmacy inventory (distinct from Return Pack, which is pharmacy-to-upstream).
An observed EPCIS event failure error code (e.g. 'SSCCs not found in system: <code>'), shown in the Failed-event error bottom sheet.

testing.idScheme: EPTTS-M-<FEATURE>-TC-<NNN> (e.g. EPTTS-M-LOGIN-TC-001); the 'M' denotes Mobile to distinguish from any web/EPTTS test suites; FEATURE is an uppercase short slug for the feature/module (LOGIN, PHARMACY-DISPENSE, DISTRIBUTOR-CREATE-SHIPMENT, INSPECTOR-TRACE, PATIENT-VALIDATE, etc.); NNN is a zero-padded 3-digit sequence per feature.
testing.tableFormat: Each test case is a Markdown file/table with: Test ID, Title, Module/Role (Pharmacy/Branch/Distributor/Inspector/Patient), Platform (Android / iOS / Both — mandatory per test-writing rules), Preconditions (login role/account, online/offline state, existing data such as an available invoice/shipment/pack), Steps (numbered, one user action or validation point per step), Expected Result per step or at the end, Priority (P1-P4), and Status. Scan-related test cases must note whether a physical scanner or the camera/manual-entry path is used. Offline/online state must be explicitly declared whenever the case touches sync-sensitive flows (Receive, Dispense, Return, Create/Receive Shipment, EPCIS History).
testing.stepStyle: Steps are written as short, literal, numbered user actions matching the actual on-screen labels and content-desc values discovered via Appium exploration (e.g. 'Tap Sign In', 'Enter credentials for <role>', 'Tap Receive Invoice', 'Tap Scan Barcode', 'Scan pack barcode X', 'Verify progress bar shows 1/3', 'Tap Initiate Return'). Each step covers exactly one user action or one validation point (per testcase-writing-rules.md) — no compound steps. Preconditions specify the exact test account/role and any required app state (e.g. an existing Dispatched invoice, a PENDING return, a pack already in pharmacy inventory). Expected results are stated precisely against the verified UI text/labels captured in the workflow.md files (e.g. exact button/tab labels, status badge text such as CONFIRMED/PENDING/CANCELLED, Completed/Failed, Draft/Dispatched/Delivered/Partially Delivered) rather than paraphrased.
testing.priorityScale: P1 = Critical/core happy-path flow for a role (e.g. Login, Pharmacy Dispense, Distributor Create Shipment, Inspector Trace, Patient Validate Pack) — must-pass before release. P2 = Secondary/supporting flows (e.g. Return Pack, Branch Return, My Returns, EPCIS History, Returns sub-menu detail actions). P3-P4 = Edge cases, validation-rule checks, and rarely-hit states (empty lists, duplicate scans, invalid barcodes, network errors, token-expiry/Unauthorized handling) — most of these are currently marked '(To be discovered through testing)' in the source docs and should be fleshed out as exploration continues.
testing.coverage: Coverage should span, per role, the full happy path plus the edge cases already enumerated in each feature's workflow.md: invalid/unrecognized barcodes, duplicate scans ('Already scanned'), pack not in inventory / already dispensed / already returned, partial completion (Partially Delivered shipments, partial return acceptance), empty-state lists, network/server errors with retry, and status-filter edge cases (e.g. Failed filter with none present). Include the shared/cross-cutting flows once per suite rather than per role where UI is identical: Logout (confirmation dialog Confirm/Cancel), Delete Account (destructive confirmation), and 15-minute token-expiry/Unauthorized handling (Retry button is known non-functional — flag as a bug candidate rather than expected behavior). GS1 scan test cases should be covered for both the camera-scan path and, where a physical scanner is used, that path noted separately. Both Android and iOS should be covered explicitly per the 'platform' rule, even though iOS capabilities/device are not yet verified live (appium-capabilities.json iOS udid is a placeholder).

bugs.formatSections: Bug reports use a front-matter + body Markdown template (bugs/_template.md): YAML front matter with title, app (eptts-mobile), feature (feature slug), severity (Critical/High/Medium/Low), priority (P1-P4), platform (Android/iOS/Both), device (Device Model - OS Version), appVersion, status (defaults to Open), reportedBy, date. Body sections in order: Summary (1-3 paragraphs describing what's broken, context, and impact), Steps to Reproduce (numbered, starting with the login role, then the module/screen, then the specific actions, ending with what to observe), Expected Result (one clear sentence), Actual Result (one clear sentence), and Environment (Device + OS version, Platform, App Version, Role/Account, Network state — Online/Offline/Both).
bugs.severityConventions: Severity: Critical / High / Medium / Low. Priority: P1 / P4 (P1 highest). Severity should reflect supply-chain/compliance impact given this is a regulated pharmaceutical track-and-trace app — e.g. an EPCIS event silently failing to submit, a pack being dispensable when it shouldn't be, or a return being confirmed twice would be Critical/High; cosmetic issues or copy mismatches on rarely used screens (e.g. Inspector detail labels) would be Low. Known non-functional Retry button on token-expiry ('Unauthorized' state after the 15-minute access-token expiry, no auto-refresh) is a good example candidate bug worth logging at High severity given it blocks all in-progress work until re-login. Each bug report must record whether the issue occurred Online or Offline and which role/account reproduced it, since behavior (and correctness) differs materially per role (Pharmacy/Branch/Distributor/Inspector/Patient).
